steps.details: Bake until golden brown and firm to the touch, 14 to 18 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the center should come out clean.

steps.title: Whip the cream
steps.details: While the biscuits bake, whip chilled cream with 2 tbsp sugar and vanilla to soft-to-medium peaks that hold their shape. Refrigerate until serving.

steps.title: Cool the biscuits
steps.details: Transfer baked biscuits to a rack and cool until warm but easy to handle, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Split and fill
steps.details: Split each biscuit horizontally with a serrated knife. Spoon macerated berries and juices over the bottom halves, add a generous dollop of whipped cream, cap with the tops, and serve immediately.

recipe.title: Fresh Lemonade
recipe.intro: You'll need a pitcher, a citrus juicer or reamer, a small saucepan, and a long spoon. Chill the water and lemons ahead if possible; roll each lemon firmly on the counter before juicing to get more juice.
recipe.finish: Taste and adjust: stir in more simple syrup for sweeter lemonade or more cold water for a lighter pour. Serve over plenty of ice; keep the pitcher in the shade or a cooler and stir before each refill.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.prep: sliced into thin rounds, optional garnish

steps.title: Make simple syrup
steps.details: Combine 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves completely, about 3–4 minutes; do not boil.

steps.title: Juice the lemons
steps.details: While the syrup heats, roll and juice the lemons until you have 1 cup of juice, then strain out seeds and pulp.

steps.title: Cool the syrup
steps.details: Remove the syrup from the heat and let it cool in the saucepan for 10 minutes so it doesn't melt all the ice.

steps.title: Combine lemonade
steps.details: Pour the cooled syrup and 1 cup lemon juice into a pitcher, add 6 cups cold water, and stir well.

steps.title: Chill and taste
steps.details: Refrigerate the pitcher for at least 20 minutes, then taste and stir in a little more sugar or water if needed.

steps.title: Serve over ice
steps.details: Fill glasses with ice, pour the lemonade over the top, and garnish with lemon slices.

recipe.title: Mummy-Wrapped Mini Hot Dogs
recipe.intro: Perfect for a Halloween party. You need a baking sheet, parchment paper, a knife or pizza cutter, and a small bowl for the egg wash. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) with a rack in the middle while you wrap. Keep the crescent dough chilled until you're ready to use it.
recipe.finish: The mummies are done when the dough is deep golden brown and puffed and the sausages are heated through (165°F/74°C if checked). Let them cool on the pan for 2–3 minutes, then serve warm with yellow mustard for dipping. If making ahead, reheat at 350°F for 5 minutes.

ingredients.name: refrigerated crescent roll dough
ingredients.prep: keep chilled until ready to use

ingredients.name: cocktail sausages (mini hot dogs), about 2 inches long
egg
ingredients.prep: beaten with 1 tbsp water for egg wash

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.prep: for dusting the work surface, optional

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.details: Set a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

steps.title: Prep the sausages
steps.details: Drain the cocktail sausages and pat them dry with a paper towel so the dough sticks. Set them on a plate.

steps.title: Mix the egg wash
steps.details: In a small bowl, beat the egg with 1 tablespoon water until smooth. Set aside.

steps.title: Cut the dough into strips
steps.details: Unroll the crescent dough onto a lightly floured surface. Press the perforations closed, then cut the dough into 24 thin strips (about 1/4 inch wide). A pizza cutter works well. Keep the dough cold.

steps.title: Wrap the mummies
steps.details: Working one at a time, wrap 1 dough strip around a sausage in a spiral, leaving a small gap near one end for the face (mummy is partially wrapped). Use 1–2 strips per sausage, overlapping loosely as you go. Place on the lined baking sheet seam-side down, about 1 inch apart.

steps.title: Brush with egg wash
steps.details: Lightly brush the wrapped dough with egg wash. This helps the mummies brown evenly and stick together.

steps.title: Bake the mummies
steps.details: Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 12–15 minutes, until the dough is deep golden brown and puffed and the sausages are hot (165°F/74°C). Rotate the pan halfway through for even browning.

steps.title: Cool and serve
steps.details: Let the mummies rest on the pan for 2–3 minutes, then transfer to a platter. Serve warm with yellow mustard for dipping.

recipe.title: Pumpkin-Shaped Cheese Ball
recipe.intro: Soften the cream cheese on the counter for 30 minutes. Have a large sheet of plastic wrap ready. No special equipment needed beyond a mixing bowl and a rubber spatula. Serve with extra crackers or vegetable sticks alongside.
recipe.finish: The cheese ball is ready when firm and cold, about 2 hours; it holds well up to 24 hours wrapped in the fridge. Just before serving, press the green bell pepper stem into the top center and gently score shallow vertical lines down the sides with the back of a knife to mimic pumpkin ridges. Let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes so it spreads easily. Serve with crackers or vegetable sticks.

ingredients.name: small green bell pepper
ingredients.prep: cut into a 1-inch stem piece, seeds removed

steps.title: Soften cream cheese
steps.details: Set the cream cheese out on the counter for 30 minutes until it yields easily to a light press. Meanwhile, crush the crackers and prep the other ingredients.

steps.title: Crush crackers and prep
steps.details: Crush the crackers into fine crumbs in a zip-top bag with a rolling pin or in a food processor and spread on a plate. Slice the green onions, drain the pumpkin puree, and cut the bell pepper stem piece.

steps.title: Beat cream cheese base
steps.details: In a large bowl, beat the softened cream cheese with the pumpkin puree, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper until smooth and evenly orange.

steps.title: Mix in cheddar and onions
steps.details: Fold in the shredded cheddar and sliced green onions until evenly distributed. Taste and adjust salt if needed.

steps.title: Chill the mixture
steps.details: Scrape the mixture onto a large sheet of plastic wrap, gather the wrap, and shape into a rough ball. Chill for 30 minutes so it firms enough to coat.

steps.title: Shape and coat in crackers
steps.details: Unwrap the chilled cheese mixture and roll it into a round ball, then roll it in the crushed crackers, pressing gently so the crumbs adhere all over and the ball looks like a pumpkin.

steps.title: Chill until firm
steps.details: Return the coated cheese ball to the fridge on a plate, covered loosely, for at least 2 hours or up to 24 hours. It is ready when firm to the touch and cold throughout.

steps.title: Add stem and serve
steps.details: Press the green bell pepper stem into the top center, score shallow vertical ridges down the sides with the back of a knife, and let sit 15 minutes at room temperature before serving with crackers.

recipe.title: Witches' Brew Punch
recipe.intro: No cooking needed—just chilling, stirring, and a spooky gummy-worm ice block. You'll need a large punch bowl or 3-quart pitcher, a freezer, and a bowl or small container that fits inside your punch bowl to freeze the worm ice. Chill all liquids beforehand so the punch stays cold and fizzy.
recipe.finish: Ladle into cups and top each glass with a few gummy worms from the ice block as it melts. Serve immediately while fizzy; if the punch sits out, add more ice and stir gently to keep it cold.

ingredients.name: gummy worms
ingredients.prep: divide: about 3/4 cup for the ice, 1/4 cup for garnish

ingredients.name: green food coloring
ingredients.prep: optional, for a brighter green tint

steps.title: Freeze gummy-worm ice block
steps.details: Put about 3/4 cup of the gummy worms in a small freezer-safe bowl or container, add 2 cups of the cold water, and freeze for at least 3 hours, or until solid. This spooky ice block will float in the punch and slowly release the worms.

steps.title: Stir limeade concentrate
steps.details: In the punch bowl or a large pitcher, stir the thawed limeade concentrate with the remaining 4 cups cold water until completely dissolved.

steps.title: Add apple juice and coloring
steps.details: Pour in the chilled apple juice and stir well. If you want a brighter witchy green, add 2 to 3 drops of green food coloring and stir until evenly tinted.

steps.title: Chill the punch base
steps.details: Cover and refrigerate the punch base until well chilled, at least 30 minutes. This keeps the drink cold so the soda stays fizzy when added.

steps.title: Add soda and worm ice
steps.details: Just before serving, pour in the chilled lemon-lime soda and stir gently once or twice—don't overmix or it will go flat. Unmold the gummy-worm ice block by dipping the container briefly in warm water, then float it in the punch. Add ice cubes if you like.

recipe.title: Slow-Cooker Spider Cider
recipe.intro: Warm spiced apple cider for a crowd, kept hot in a 4- to 6-quart slow cooker. You'll need a vegetable peeler, a small paring knife, and a fine-mesh strainer or slotted spoon. No specialty gear required. Start about 2½ hours before guests arrive; the cider holds on Warm all evening.
recipe.finish: Ladle into mugs, leaving the whole spices behind with a strainer or slotted spoon. Garnish each mug with a fresh orange slice and one cinnamon stick laid across the rim as a "leg." Keep the slow cooker on Warm (at least 140°F/60°C) while serving and stir every 30–45 minutes. Discard any cider left out at room temperature longer than 2 hours.

ingredients.name: apple cider
ingredients.prep: shake or stir well before pouring

ingredients.name: orange peel
ingredients.prep: peeled with a vegetable peeler, white pith avoided

ingredients.name: cinnamon sticks
ingredients.prep: left whole, plus extra for garnish

ingredients.name: honey or maple syrup
ingredients.prep: measured; add to taste after tasting

ingredients.name: orange
ingredients.prep: sliced into thin rounds for garnish

steps.title: Pour cider into slow cooker
steps.details: Pour the gallon of cider into a 4- to 6-quart slow cooker. Stir in the honey or maple syrup until dissolved.

steps.title: Peel and slice the orange
steps.details: While the cider starts heating, peel 3 long strips from the orange with a vegetable peeler, avoiding the bitter white pith. Then slice the orange into thin rounds and set aside for garnish.

steps.title: Add spices to cider
steps.details: Add the orange peel strips, 6 whole cloves, 4 cinnamon sticks, and the star anise (if using) to the cider. Stir once.

steps.title: Heat cider on High
steps.details: Cover and cook on High until steaming and hot but not boiling, about 45–60 minutes. Check with an instant-read thermometer: it should reach at least 165°F (74°C). Do not let it boil, which makes the cider taste flat.

steps.title: Steep on Low
steps.details: Turn the slow cooker to Low and steep 60–90 minutes so the spices infuse. Keep the lid on to hold heat. The cider is ready when it smells strongly of cinnamon and tastes spiced; taste and stir in a little more honey if it needs sweetness.

steps.title: Strain out whole spices
steps.details: Just before serving, fish out the orange peel, cloves, star anise, and steeped cinnamon sticks with a slotted spoon or strainer. Discard them. Turn the slow cooker to Warm (at least 140°F/60°C).

steps.title: Set out garnishes
steps.details: Arrange the orange slices and 8–12 fresh cinnamon sticks near the slow cooker for guests to garnish. Ladle cider into mugs and add one orange slice and one cinnamon stick "leg" to each.

recipe.title: Bat Wing Buffalo Wings
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on top; coat rack with cooking spray. Pat wings very dry with paper towels for crisp skin. Have a basting brush and tongs ready.
recipe.finish: Wings are done when an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the meat, away from bone, reads 175°F (79°C) and skin is crisp and golden. Toss or brush with the glossy buffalo glaze, then arrange wings in pairs on a platter with the two small drumette bones pointing up like bat wings and add a few black sesame seeds for eyes if desired. Serve warm with celery and blue cheese dressing.

ingredients.name: chicken wings, split into flats and drumettes
ingredients.prep: pat dry, discard tips or save for stock

ingredients.name: black sesame seeds or whole black peppercorns

steps.title: Heat oven and rack
steps.details: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and position rack in upper-middle. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on it; coat rack with cooking spray.

steps.title: Dry and season wings
steps.details: Pat wings very dry. In a large bowl, toss wings with baking powder, salt and pepper until evenly coated; the light dusting helps the skin crisp.

steps.title: Arrange on rack
steps.details: Spread wings skin-side up on the prepared rack in a single layer, not touching. Discard any leftover seasoning in the bowl.

steps.title: Bake until crisp
steps.details: Bake 40–45 minutes, turning once halfway through, until skin is crisp and golden and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest meat away from bone reads 175°F (79°C).

steps.title: Make buffalo glaze
steps.details: While wings bake, melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir in hot sauce, honey and garlic powder; keep warm, not simmering.

steps.title: Toss wings in glaze
steps.details: Transfer hot crisp wings to a large clean bowl, pour over warm buffalo glaze, and toss or brush until glossy and evenly coated.

steps.title: Plate as bat wings
steps.details: Arrange glazed wings in pairs on a platter with the two small drumette bones pointing upward like bat wings; dot with black sesame seeds for eyes if using. Serve warm.

recipe.title: Jack-o'-Lantern Stuffed Peppers
recipe.intro: Heat oven to 375°F. You will need a 9x13-inch baking dish, a skillet, and a small paring knife. Cook rice and brown beef while you carve the peppers so nothing sits idle.
recipe.finish: Peppers are done when the flesh is tender when pierced with a knife and the filling registers at least 165°F. Let rest 5 minutes, then serve hot with the lids alongside or on top.

ingredients.name: orange bell peppers
ingredients.prep: halve tops off, remove seeds and membranes, carve simple pumpkin faces

steps.title: Preheat oven
steps.details: Set oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle position.

steps.title: Carve the peppers
steps.details: Cut the top 1/2 inch off each pepper and set the tops aside. Scoop out seeds and membranes. With a paring knife, cut two triangle eyes, a small triangle nose, and a zigzag mouth through the front wall of each pepper. Keep the pieces small; discard the cutouts.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.details: Combine rice and water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low until water is absorbed and rice is tender, about 18 minutes. Let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.details: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook the beef with the onion, breaking it up, until no pink remains and the onion is soft, 7 to 9 minutes. Drain excess fat.

steps.title: Season the filling
steps.details: Add garlic, oregano, salt, pepper, and drained diced tomatoes to the skillet. Cook 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.

steps.title: Combine filling
steps.details: Stir the cooked rice and 1/2 cup of the cheddar into the beef mixture until evenly combined.

steps.title: Stuff the peppers
steps.details: Stand the carved peppers upright in the baking dish. Spoon the filling into each pepper, packing gently and mounding slightly. Top each with some of the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar. Set the reserved pepper tops on or beside the peppers.

steps.title: Bake the peppers
steps.details: Pour 1/2 cup water into the bottom of the dish, cover tightly with foil, and bake 35 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until a knife slides easily into the pepper flesh and the filling reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.details: Remove from oven and rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipe.title: Mummy Meat Loaf
recipe.intro: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Use a rimmed baking sheet lined with foil or parchment. Have a food thermometer ready. Mix the meat loaf base while the oven preheats.
recipe.finish: Let the loaf rest 10 minutes before slicing so juices stay in. The bacon should be browned and crisp at the edges and the center must read 160°F (71°C). Serve in thick slices with ketchup or gravy on the side.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep pan
steps.details: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.

steps.title: Soak breadcrumbs
steps.details: Stir the breadcrumbs into the milk in a large bowl and let sit 5 minutes until moistened.

steps.title: Add onion and seasonings
steps.details: Add the diced onion, beaten eggs, ketchup, Worcestershire, salt and pepper to the soaked crumbs and stir to combine.

steps.title: Mix in beef
steps.details: Add the ground beef and mix gently with your hands just until evenly combined; do not overwork it.

steps.title: Shape the loaf
steps.details: Turn the mixture onto the lined pan and shape into a domed loaf about 9 by 5 inches and 2 inches high.

steps.title: Drape bacon bandages
steps.details: Lay bacon strips across the loaf at slight angles, overlapping like mummy bandages and tucking the ends under the loaf.

steps.title: Bake the loaf
steps.details: Bake until the bacon is browned and crisp at the edges and the center reads 160°F (71°C), about 55 to 65 minutes.

steps.title: Add olive eyes
steps.details: Press the olive halves, cut side down, into the top of the loaf near one end to make two eyes.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.details: Let the loaf rest 10 minutes, then slice thickly and serve.

recipe.title: Monster Mash Potatoes
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 200°F (95°C) to keep finished potatoes warm if needed. You need a large pot, colander, potato masher or ricer, sturdy piping bag with a large star tip (or a zip-top bag with a corner snipped), and a rimmed baking sheet. Have all ingredients ready before mashing so the potatoes stay hot.
recipe.finish: The mounds are done when piping holds sharp ridges and the peas are warmed through. If potatoes cooled and look stiff, rewarm the tray 5 minutes at 325°F (165°C); do not let the butter brown. Serve hot, spooning any pooled butter from the tray over the monsters.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.prep: for the boiling water, plus more to taste

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.details: Put the potato chunks in a large pot and add cool water to cover by 2 inches. Stir in the 1 tbsp kosher salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook until a knife slides through a chunk with no resistance, 15 to 18 minutes.

steps.title: Warm milk and butter
steps.details: While the potatoes boil, combine the 6 tbsp butter and the milk in a small saucepan over low heat until the butter melts and the milk is hot but not simmering, about 5 minutes. Keep warm off the heat.

steps.title: Drain and dry potatoes
steps.details: Pour the potatoes into a colander and drain well. Return them to the dry pot over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes, shaking, until the surface looks dry and steamy. This removes excess water so the mash stays fluffy.

steps.title: Mash and enrich
steps.details: Mash the hot potatoes until mostly smooth. Add the warm milk-butter mixture, sour cream, and black pepper. Stir gently until creamy and no dry streaks remain; taste and add salt if needed. Do not overbeat or the potatoes turn gluey.

steps.title: Load the piping bag
steps.details: Fit the star tip into the piping bag and set it tip-down in a tall glass. Spoon in the hot potatoes, filling no more than two-thirds full. Twist the top closed and squeeze once to release any air pocket.

steps.title: Pipe spooky mounds
steps.details: Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Pipe 8 mounds about 3 inches wide and 2 inches tall, swirling upward to a peak. Leave 1 inch between mounds. Work in batches if the bag gets hard to squeeze.

steps.title: Add pea eyes
steps.details: Press 2 or 3 thawed peas into the side of each mound as eyes, pushing gently so they stick. Keep peas near the top so they show.

steps.title: Warm through and drizzle
steps.details: Bake the tray at 300°F (150°C) until the mounds are hot in the center, 10 to 12 minutes. A thermometer should read 165°F (74°C). Drizzle the 2 tbsp melted butter over the tops just before serving.

recipe.title: Roasted Pumpkin and Brussels Sprouts
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) with racks in upper and lower thirds. Have two rimmed baking sheets ready. Use a sharp knife and stable cutting board; keep pumpkin pieces and sprouts similar size for even roasting.
recipe.finish: Pumpkin should be fork-tender with caramelized edges and sprouts tender-crisp with browned outer leaves. Taste and add salt or a drizzle of maple syrup if needed. Transfer to a warm platter and serve immediately; this side is best fresh but holds 20 minutes loosely tented with foil.

ingredients.name: pumpkin, sugar pie or butternut squash

steps.title: Heat oven and prep vegetables
steps.details: Set oven to 425°F (220°C). While it heats, peel, seed, and cube the pumpkin into 1-inch pieces, and trim and halve the Brussels sprouts lengthwise through the core.

steps.title: Season pumpkin
steps.details: On one rimmed baking sheet, toss pumpkin cubes with 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper until evenly coated. Spread into a single layer with space between pieces.

steps.title: Season Brussels sprouts
steps.details: On the second rimmed baking sheet, toss halved sprouts with the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper. Arrange cut-side down in a single layer.

steps.title: Roast pumpkin
steps.details: Place pumpkin on the upper rack and roast until fork-tender and caramelized at the edges, 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway through.

steps.title: Roast Brussels sprouts
steps.details: Place sprouts on the lower rack and roast until tender-crisp and browned on the cut sides, 22–28 minutes, shaking the pan once halfway through.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.details: Test pumpkin and sprouts with a fork; pumpkin should yield easily and sprouts should be tender at the core with crisp browned leaves. If needed, roast 3–5 minutes more, checking every 2 minutes.

steps.title: Combine and finish
steps.details: Transfer both vegetables to a serving platter, sprinkle with fresh thyme if using, and gently toss. Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot.

recipe.title: Graveyard Dirt Cups
recipe.intro: Make-ahead no-bake Halloween dessert. You need 6 clear cups (8–10 oz), a zip-top bag and a rolling pin or food processor. Use instant chocolate pudding and cold milk; keep pudding cold until serving.
recipe.finish: Cups are ready when chilled at least 30 minutes and pudding is set. Serve cold; add gummy worms and tombstone just before serving so cookies stay crunchy. Store covered in the fridge up to 1 day.

steps.title: Crush cookies for dirt
steps.details: Put 12 chocolate sandwich cookies in a zip-top bag and crush with a rolling pin into coarse crumbs with some pea-size pieces (or pulse in a food processor). Set aside.

steps.title: Whisk pudding and milk
steps.details: In a medium bowl, whisk the instant pudding mix into the cold milk for 2 minutes until smooth and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Chill pudding to set
steps.details: Refrigerate the pudding, uncovered, until set, about 30 minutes. It should hold its shape when spooned.

steps.title: Layer cups with dirt
steps.details: Spoon about 2 tablespoons pudding into each cup, top with 1 tablespoon crushed cookies, then repeat once so each cup has two pudding layers and two crumb layers, ending with crumbs.

steps.title: Add worms and tombstones
steps.details: Press 2 gummy worms into the top dirt of each cup, half-buried. Stand 1 whole cookie upright in each cup as a tombstone, pressing gently into the crumbs.

steps.title: Chill before serving
steps.details: Refrigerate the cups until cold, at least 20 minutes, then serve.

recipe.title: Herb-Roasted Bone-In Turkey Breast
recipe.intro: Let the turkey breast sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before roasting. Heat oven to 375°F (190°C) with a rack in the lower-middle position. You need a roasting pan with a rack or a rimmed baking sheet with a wire rack, a small bowl, and an instant-read thermometer. Pat the turkey very dry with paper towels so the herb rub sticks and the skin
recipe.finish: The turkey is done when the thickest part of the breast reads 160°F (71°C) and the juices run clear; carryover heat will bring it to 165°F. Rest 15 minutes before slicing, which also makes it easier to transport. Slice across the grain and pour the defatted pan juices over the top. To travel, slice and pack in a lidded dish with juices, keeping it warm or chilling it safely and reheating to 165°F.

steps.title: Heat oven and dry turkey
steps.details: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Pat the turkey breast very dry inside and out with paper towels and place it skin-side up on a rack in a roasting pan.

steps.title: Mix herb butter
steps.details: Mash the softened butter with the minced garlic, thyme, sage, salt, and pepper until it forms a paste.

steps.title: Rub and roast
steps.details: Loosen the skin over the breast and spread half the herb butter underneath. Rub the rest all over the outside, then drizzle with olive oil. Scatter onion wedges in the pan and pour in 1/2 cup broth. Roast uncovered for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Baste and continue roasting
steps.details: Spoon pan juices over the breast and add the remaining 1/2 cup broth if the pan looks dry. Continue roasting 45 to 60 minutes, basting once more, until the thickest part of the breast reads 160°F (71°C) on an instant-read thermometer.

steps.title: Rest before slicing
steps.details: Transfer the turkey to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Rest 15 minutes; the temperature will rise to 165°F. Meanwhile, skim the fat from the pan juices and keep the onion wedges for serving.

steps.title: Carve and serve
steps.details: Slice the breast across the grain, discarding the bone. Arrange on a platter with the onion wedges and spoon the defatted pan juices over the top.

recipe.title: Slow-Cooker Cranberry-Orange Sauce
recipe.intro: No special gear beyond a 4- to 6-quart slow cooker and a vegetable peeler. This sauce is made the night before or morning of the potluck and transported in the slow cooker set to Warm, so it stays glossy and ready to serve straight from the pot.
recipe.finish: Sauce is done when berries have burst and the liquid is thick enough to mound slightly on a spoon; it will thicken more as it cools. Fish out the cinnamon stick, pot it in the slow cooker on Warm, and serve with roast turkey or ham. Keeps 5 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen; thin with a splash of orange juice if it tightens too much on Warm.

ingredients.name: orange juice
ingredients.prep: squeeze from 1 orange if not using bottled

ingredients.name: orange zest
ingredients.prep: peel with a vegetable peeler, avoiding white pith

steps.title: Combine sugar and liquids
steps.details: In the slow cooker, stir together the sugar, orange juice, water, and salt until the sugar is dissolved and no dry clumps remain.

steps.title: Add zest and cinnamon
steps.details: Add the orange zest and cinnamon stick and give them a quick stir so they sit under the liquid and infuse evenly during cooking.

steps.title: Stir in cranberries
steps.details: Add all the cranberries and stir until evenly coated. They will not be submerged at first; that is fine, the sauce is stirred once partway through.

steps.title: Slow-cook on Low
steps.details: Cover and cook on Low until the berries have popped and the liquid is thick enough to mound slightly on a spoon, 2 to 3 hours. Stir once after 1 1/2 hours, then check every 30 minutes; if the cooker lid does not seal well, err toward the longer end.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.details: Run a spoon across the bottom of the pot: if the sauce holds a brief trail before slowly filling in, it is done. If it is still watery, uncover and cook on High 15 to 30 minutes more to reduce.

steps.title: Uncover and cool slightly
steps.details: Turn off the cooker, remove the lid, and let the sauce sit 10 minutes. This lets it thicken to a glossy, spoonable consistency and cool enough to taste.

steps.title: Remove aromatics and taste
steps.details: Fish out the cinnamon stick and the orange zest strip with a spoon. Taste and adjust: more sugar if the cranberries were very tart, a little more orange juice if it tastes too thick.

steps.title: Hold on Warm for serving
steps.details: Cover and hold on Warm (at least 140°F) until serving, stirring every 30 minutes to keep the surface glossy; keep it on Warm no more than 3 hours before the potluck. If made ahead and chilled, reheat on High to 165°F, then set to Warm.

recipe.title: Brown Butter Mashed Potatoes
recipe.intro: Peel and cut potatoes into 1-inch chunks. Have a colander, large pot, and small light-colored skillet ready. No specialty equipment needed.
recipe.finish: Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Keep warm until serving, or cover and reheat gently with a splash more milk.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.details: Put the potatoes and 1 tbsp salt in a large pot and add cold water to cover by 1 inch. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook 15–18 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.details: While the potatoes cook, melt the butter in a small light-colored skillet over medium heat. Swirl and cook 3–5 minutes until the milk solids turn golden brown and smell nutty; remove from heat.

steps.title: Warm the milk
steps.details: Gently warm the milk in a small saucepan or microwave until steaming but not boiling. Keep warm.

steps.title: Drain the potatoes
steps.details: Drain the potatoes well in a colander and return them to the hot, dry pot. Let them sit 1–2 minutes to steam off excess moisture.

steps.title: Mash with sour cream
steps.details: Add the sour cream and mash until smooth, or use a ricer or masher to the texture you like. Do not overwork.

steps.title: Add brown butter and milk
steps.details: Pour in the browned butter with its browned bits and half the warm milk. Stir until combined, adding more milk until creamy.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.details: Stir in the kosher salt and pepper. Taste and adjust. Serve hot.

recipe.title: Sausage and Apple Stuffing
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 350°F. You need a large rimmed baking sheet, a large skillet, and a 9x13-inch baking dish. Use store-bought unseasoned bread cubes or tear a 1-pound loaf of day-old bread into 1/2-inch cubes. Have everything diced and chopped before you start cooking so the timeline flows.
recipe.finish: Stuffing is done when the top is golden brown and the center registers 165°F on an instant-read thermometer, 40–45 minutes. If the top browns too fast, tent loosely with foil. Let rest 10 minutes before serving; it holds well covered at 200°F for up to 1 hour at a potluck.

ingredients.name: unseasoned bread cubes
ingredients.prep: spread in a single layer if not already dried

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.prep: warmed in a saucepan or microwave

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.prep: melted, plus extra for the dish

steps.title: Toast the bread cubes
steps.details: Spread bread cubes on a large rimmed baking sheet. Bake at 350°F, stirring once halfway, until dry and lightly toasted, 12–15 minutes. Set aside; leave oven on.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.details: While the bread toasts, heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add sausage and cook, breaking it up, until browned and no longer pink, 8–10 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl with a slotted spoon, leaving about 1 tablespoon of fat in the pan.

steps.title: Soften vegetables and apples
steps.details: Add onion and celery to the skillet; cook over medium heat until softened, about 6 minutes. Add apples and cook until just tender, 4–5 minutes more. Stir in garlic, sage, thyme, salt, and pepper; cook 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Combine stuffing mixture
steps.details: In the large bowl, combine toasted bread cubes, sausage, and the skillet mixture. Toss until evenly distributed. Whisk broth, eggs, and melted butter together, then pour over the bread mixture and toss gently until all cubes are moistened.

steps.title: Bake the stuffing
steps.details: Butter a 9x13-inch baking dish and pack in the stuffing. Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake until golden on top and the center reaches 165°F, 15–20 minutes more.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.details: Remove from oven and rest 10 minutes before serving. Taste and add salt if needed.

recipe.title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F with racks in upper and lower thirds. You need 2 rimmed baking sheets, a large bowl, and a skillet. Ready a large potluck platter; this travels well warm or at room temperature.
recipe.finish: Sprouts should be deeply browned at the cut edges and fork-tender, bacon crisp, and glaze glossy. Taste for salt and pepper, add the reserved bacon and an extra thin drizzle of maple syrup, and serve warm or at room temperature.

steps.title: Preheat and prep sprouts
steps.details: Heat oven to 425°F. Trim and halve 2 lb sprouts; keep any loose leaves. Whisk 2 tbsp olive oil with salt and pepper in a large bowl.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.details: Cook bacon pieces in a skillet over medium heat, stirring, until deeply crisp and fat is rendered, 9–11 minutes. Transfer to paper towels with a slotted spoon; reserve 1 tbsp bacon fat and set bacon aside.

steps.title: Toss sprouts with oil
steps.details: Add sprouts to the oil mixture and toss until every leaf is coated. If sprouts are dry, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.

steps.title: Roast sprouts
steps.details: Spread sprouts cut-side down on 2 rimmed sheets in a single layer. Roast 20 minutes, then swap and rotate the sheets and roast until cut edges are browned and centers are fork-tender, 8–12 minutes more.

steps.title: Whisk maple glaze
steps.details: While sprouts roast, whisk maple syrup with apple cider vinegar and the reserved 1 tbsp bacon fat in a small bowl.

steps.title: Toss with bacon and glaze
steps.details: Transfer hot sprouts to a large bowl. Add the glaze and most of the bacon; toss gently, scraping up browned bits.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.details: Taste and season with salt and pepper. Scatter the reserved bacon on top, drizzle with a little extra maple syrup, and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipe.title: Creamy Green Bean Casserole
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 350°F. You need a 9x13-inch baking dish, a large skillet, and a pot for blanching. Thaw nothing; use frozen cut green beans straight from the bag. Reserve about 1 cup of fried onions for the topping before you start.
recipe.finish: The casserole is done when the sauce bubbles at the edges and the onions are deep golden brown, about 30 minutes. Let it rest 5 minutes before serving; it will be very hot. It holds well on a potluck table for up to an hour.

steps.title: Boil water and blanch beans
steps.details: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add frozen green beans and cook 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender but still with a slight bite. Drain well and set aside.

steps.title: Sauté mushrooms and onion
steps.details: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms, diced onion, salt, and pepper. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms release their liquid, it evaporates, and the onions are soft and lightly golden.

steps.title: Add garlic and flour
steps.details: Stir in minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 1 minute to coat and cook out the raw flour taste.

steps.title: Whisk in milk and cream
steps.details: Pour in milk and cream in a steady stream while whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Add soy sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 4–5 minutes, whisking, until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Fold in beans and cheese
steps.details: Remove skillet from heat. Stir in drained green beans, 5 oz of the fried onions (about 1 1/2 cups), and the parmesan until evenly combined. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.

steps.title: Bake the casserole
steps.details: Transfer mixture to the 9x13-inch baking dish and spread evenly. Bake uncovered at 350°F for 20 minutes, until the sauce bubbles at the edges and the center is hot.

steps.title: Top with fried onions and brown
steps.details: Scatter the reserved 1 cup fried onions over the top. Return to the oven and bake 8–10 minutes more, until the onions are deep golden brown and crisp. Watch closely at the end so they do not burn.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.details: Remove from oven and let rest 5 minutes before serving. The casserole is very hot; warn guests and use a serving spoon.

recipe.title: Buttermilk Skillet Cornbread
recipe.intro: Heat oven to 425°F with a 10-inch cast-iron skillet (or 9-inch round cake pan) inside. Have a whisk, two bowls and a spatula ready; the bread bakes in about 20 minutes, so it can go in after the rest of the menu prep is underway.
recipe.finish: Cornbread is done when the top is deep golden and the center springs back when lightly pressed, or a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean (about 200°F internal), 20–24 minutes. Cool in the skillet 10 minutes, then cut into wedges. Serve warm to soak up gravy; wrap leftovers tightly at room temperature for up to 2 days.

steps.title: Heat the skillet
steps.details: Place the empty skillet (or cake pan) on the middle rack and heat the oven to 425°F. Let the skillet heat while you mix, at least 15 minutes.

steps.title: Mix dry ingredients
steps.details: Whisk cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl until evenly combined.

steps.title: Whisk wet ingredients
steps.details: In a second bowl, whisk buttermilk, eggs and melted butter until smooth and uniform.

steps.title: Fold batter together
steps.details: Pour the wet mixture into the dry bowl and fold with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain; a few small lumps are fine. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Melt fat in hot skillet
steps.details: Carefully slide the hot skillet out, add the bacon drippings or oil, and swirl to coat the bottom and sides; the fat should sizzle.

steps.title: Pour and bake
steps.details: Pour the batter into the hot skillet and spread it evenly. Return to the oven and bake until deep golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean, 20–24 minutes.

steps.title: Cool and cut
steps.details: Set the skillet on a rack and cool 10 minutes. Run a thin knife around the edge, invert or lift out, and cut into 12 wedges.

recipe.title: Spiced Pumpkin Pie Bars
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) with a rack in the middle. You need a 9x13-inch baking pan, parchment paper, a mixing bowl, a food processor or pastry cutter for the crust, and a whisk. Line the pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides. Let butter and cream cheese sit out for 20 minutes so they soften while you measure everything.
recipe.finish: Cool the bars completely in the pan on a rack, about 1 hour, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before slicing so the filling sets firm. Lift out by the parchment, cut into 24 bars with a warm knife, and serve chilled or cool. Store covered in the refrigerator up to 3 days; these travel well to a potluck.

steps.title: Heat oven and line pan
steps.details: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a 9x13-inch pan with parchment, leaving overhang on two sides, and lightly grease the exposed pan sides.

steps.title: Make the crust
steps.details: Pulse or cut flour, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon salt with cold butter until pea-sized clumps form. Press firmly into an even layer in the pan.

steps.title: Bake the crust
steps.details: Bake the crust 15–18 minutes until golden at the edges and set in the center. Set the pan on a rack but leave the oven on.

steps.title: Beat cream cheese and sugars
steps.details: While the crust bakes, beat softened cream cheese with 3/4 cup granulated sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar until smooth, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Bloom spices into filling
steps.details: Beat in 2 teaspoons cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves and 1/2 teaspoon salt until evenly combined and fragrant.

steps.title: Add eggs, pumpkin and cream
steps.details: Add eggs one at a time, then pumpkin puree, heavy cream and vanilla. Beat just until smooth; do not overmix or the filling puffs and cracks.

steps.title: Pour filling on warm crust
steps.details: Give the filling a final stir, then pour it over the warm crust and spread evenly to the edges. Tap the pan gently on the counter to release bubbles.

steps.title: Bake the bars
steps.details: Bake 35–40 minutes until the edges are set and the center jiggles only slightly when nudged. A knife inserted near the center should come out nearly clean.

steps.title: Toast pecans (optional)
steps.details: While the bars bake, spread chopped pecans on a small pan and toast 5–7 minutes until fragrant, watching closely so they do not burn.

steps.title: Cool, chill and top
steps.details: Cool completely in the pan on a rack, about 60 minutes, then refrigerate at least 2 hours. Sprinkle with toasted pecans before slicing into 24 bars.

recipe.title: Apple Cider Sangria
recipe.intro: No cooking needed—just chilling and stirring. You'll need a large 2-quart pitcher, a knife and cutting board, and a long spoon. Chill the cider and wine ahead if you can; the sangria needs at least 1 hour in the fridge before serving.
recipe.finish: Stir again, then pour over ice, spooning some fruit into each glass. Garnish with fresh orange slices and a cinnamon stick if you like. Keep any leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 2 days (fruit will soften).

ingredients.name: dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc
orange
ingredients.prep: halved and thinly sliced into half-moons

steps.title: Slice fruit and add to pitcher
steps.details: Cut the orange into thin half-moons and the apple into thin slices. Put both in the bottom of a 2-quart pitcher and add the 2 cinnamon sticks.

steps.title: Pour in cider, wine, and liqueur
steps.details: Pour the chilled apple cider, white wine, and orange liqueur (if using) over the fruit. Stir gently with a long spoon to combine.

steps.title: Chill to meld flavors
steps.details: Cover the pitcher and refrigerate at least 1 hour (up to overnight) so the fruit flavors mingle. This can be done hours ahead.

steps.title: Add fizz and serve over ice
steps.details: Just before serving, stir in the chilled club soda or ginger ale. Fill glasses with ice and pour the sangria over, including some fruit. Cue: drink is cold and gently bubbly.

generatedRecipes.title: Apple Cider Brined Roast Pork Loin

recipe.title: Apple Cider Brined Roast Pork Loin
recipe.intro: Use a boneless pork loin (not tenderloin), about 3 to 3.5 lb. You need a large pot or brining bag that fits the loin and the fridge. Start the brine the night before or at least 8 hours ahead. Bring the loin to room temperature for 30 minutes before roasting and preheat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Have a roasting pan with a rack an
recipe.finish: The pork is done when the thickest part reads 140°F to 145°F, about 15 to 20 minutes per pound. Rest it covered loosely with foil for 15 minutes; the temperature will rise to about 150°F and the juices will settle. Slice into 1/2-inch medallions and spoon the reduced pan cider over the top. Serve with roasted fall vegetables and mashed potatoes.

ingredients.name: boneless pork loin roast
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and silver skin

steps.title: Simmer the brine
steps.details: In a large pot, combine 2 cups of the apple cider, the water, 1/3 cup kosher salt, brown sugar, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, cinnamon sticks, and garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the salt and sugar dissolve, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the remaining 2 cups cold cider to cool it down.

steps.title: Chill the brine
steps.details: Cool the brine to refrigerator temperature, about 40°F. To speed this up, set the pot in a sink of ice water for 20 minutes, or refrigerate it uncovered for 2 hours. The pork must not go into warm brine.

steps.title: Brine the pork
steps.details: Put the pork loin in a large zip-top bag or snug container and pour the chilled brine over it, adding the aromatics. Seal and refrigerate for at least 8 hours and up to 24 hours, turning once halfway through.

steps.title: Dry and season the loin
steps.details: Remove the loin from the brine, discarding the brine, and pat it very dry with paper towels. Let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes. Rub all over with the olive oil, 1 tsp kosher salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Meanwhile heat the oven to 425°F.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.details: Set a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 425°F. Place a rack inside a roasting pan.

steps.title: Sear the loin
steps.details: Set the seasoned loin on the roasting rack and roast at 425°F for 15 minutes to brown the exterior. Do not open the oven during this time.

steps.title: Roast to temperature
steps.details: Reduce the oven to 350°F and continue roasting until an instant-read thermometer inserted in the thickest part reads 140°F to 145°F, about 15 to 20 minutes per pound total, roughly 35 to 45 more minutes. Check at 30 minutes, then every 5 to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Rest the pork
steps.details: Transfer the loin to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 15 minutes. The temperature will rise to about 150°F. Reserve the roasting pan with the drippings.

steps.title: Make the cider pan sauce
steps.details: Set the roasting pan over medium heat. Add the chicken broth and the remaining 2 cups apple cider, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer until reduced by half, about 8 minutes. Whisk in the flour, then the cold butter, one piece at a time, until lightly thickened. Season to taste.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.details: Slice the rested pork into 1/2-inch medallions against the grain. Arrange on a platter, spoon the warm cider sauce over the top, and serve immediately.

generatedRecipes.title: Roasted Delicata Squash with Brown Butter

recipe.title: Roasted Delicata Squash with Brown Butter
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the middle. Have two rimmed baking sheets ready. Delicata skin is thin and edible—just scrub it. Wash and dry the sage. Measure butter and cut into pieces so it browns evenly.
recipe.finish: The squash is done when the rings are deeply golden at the edges and tender when pierced with a knife, about 25–30 minutes. Drizzle the warm brown butter and crispy sage over the squash, toss gently to coat, and taste for salt. Serve hot or at room temperature as a side.

ingredients.name: delicata squash
ingredients.prep: scrub, trim ends, halve lengthwise, scoop seeds, slice into 1/2-inch half-moons

steps.title: Slice squash and prep sage
steps.details: Scrub the squash, trim ends, halve lengthwise, scoop out seeds with a spoon, and slice into 1/2-inch half-moon rings. Pat the sage leaves dry. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).

steps.title: Preheat oven
steps.details: Set oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the middle while you finish prepping the squash.

steps.title: Toss squash with oil and seasonings
steps.details: On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the squash rings with olive oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated, then spread in a single layer with space between pieces.

steps.title: Roast squash
steps.details: Roast at 425°F (220°C) on the middle rack for 12 minutes, until the bottoms begin to brown.

steps.title: Flip and continue roasting
steps.details: Flip the squash rings with a spatula and continue roasting 12–15 minutes more, until edges are deeply golden and a knife slides in easily.

steps.title: Brown butter with sage
steps.details: Melt the butter in a small light-colored skillet over medium heat. When it foams, add the sage leaves and cook, swirling, 2–3 minutes until the butter turns amber-brown with a nutty aroma and the sage is crisp. Pull off the heat immediately so it doesn't scorch.

steps.title: Toss squash in brown butter
steps.details: Drizzle the warm brown butter and crispy sage over the hot roasted squash on the sheet, toss gently to coat, and taste for salt. Serve immediately.

recipe.title: Maple-Glazed Brussels Sprouts
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the upper third. Have a large rimmed baking sheet ready. Rinse and trim the sprouts, then cut them in half lengthwise so they roast evenly and catch the glaze.
recipe.finish: Sprouts should be deeply browned at the edges and fork-tender, and the glaze should look glossy and sticky. Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed, then transfer to a serving bowl and serve warm.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.details: Set oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the upper third. Let it come fully up to temperature while you prep the sprouts.

steps.title: Prep the sprouts
steps.details: Trim the stem ends and cut each sprout in half lengthwise. Pull off any loose or wilted outer leaves. Keep the halves similar in size for even roasting.

steps.title: Season and spread
steps.details: On the baking sheet, toss the sprout halves with olive oil, salt and pepper until evenly coated, then arrange them cut-side down in a single layer with a little space between them.

steps.title: Roast until browned
steps.details: Roast on the upper rack for 20 minutes, until the cut sides are deeply browned and the sprouts are nearly fork-tender. Shake the pan once halfway through for even browning.

steps.title: Mix the maple glaze
steps.details: While the sprouts roast, stir together the maple syrup, butter and cider vinegar in a small bowl so the butter is ready to melt into the hot pan.

steps.title: Add glaze and finish roasting
steps.details: Pull the hot pan from the oven, drizzle the maple mixture over the sprouts and toss gently to coat. Return to the oven for 5–6 minutes, until the glaze is sticky and the sprouts are fully fork-tender. Watch closely so the syrup does not scorch.

recipe.title: Wild Rice and Mushroom Pilaf
recipe.intro: Use a 3-quart saucepan with a lid and a large skillet. Rinse the wild rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold water until the water runs clear. Have all ingredients chopped and measured before starting.
recipe.finish: Fluff the rice with a fork. The wild rice should be split open and chewy-tender, and the mushrooms deeply browned. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Serve hot alongside roasted meats or poultry; it holds well covered off heat for 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: cremini mushrooms
ingredients.prep: brushed clean and sliced 1/4 inch thick

steps.title: Simmer the wild rice
steps.details: In the saucepan, combine the rinsed wild rice, broth, and salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until the grains are split open and chewy-tender, 45 to 50 minutes. Do not stir during cooking.

steps.title: Sauté the mushrooms
steps.details: While the rice simmers, heat 2 tablespoons butter and the olive oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook without stirring for 4 minutes, then stir and continue until browned and their moisture has evaporated, about 6 more minutes.

steps.title: Add onion and garlic
steps.details: Push the mushrooms to the side of the skillet. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon butter and the onion and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, thyme, and pepper and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Check rice doneness
steps.details: Uncover the rice and taste a few grains; they should be split and tender with a slight chew. If still firm, add 1/4 cup hot water, cover, and simmer 5 minutes more. Most of the liquid should be absorbed.

steps.title: Combine rice and mushrooms
steps.details: Scrape the mushroom mixture into the saucepan with the rice. Stir gently over low heat for 2 minutes so the flavors meld and any remaining broth is absorbed.

steps.title: Rest and finish with parsley
steps.details: Remove from heat, cover, and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, fold in the parsley, taste, and adjust salt and pepper before serving.

recipe.title: Butternut Squash and Apple Soup
recipe.intro: Peel and cube the squash and apples, chop the onion, and measure the broth and cream before starting. Use a large pot and a blender or immersion blender. No preheat needed.
recipe.finish: Soup is done when the squash and apples mash easily with a spoon; blend until silky and season to taste. Serve hot with a swirl of cream or toasted pumpkin seeds if you like.

steps.title: Sweat the onion
steps.details: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and translucent, about 6 minutes.

steps.title: Add squash and apples
steps.details: Stir in the squash, apples, salt, pepper, and cinnamon. Cook, stirring, for 2 minutes to coat and start softening.

steps.title: Simmer until tender
steps.details: Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a gentle simmer, cover partly, and cook until the squash and apples mash easily with a spoon, 18 to 22 minutes.

steps.title: Blend until silky
steps.details: Remove from heat. Blend with an immersion blender until completely smooth, or blend in batches in a countertop blender with the lid vented.

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.details: Stir in the heavy cream and warm over low heat for 3 minutes without boiling. Taste and adjust salt and pepper, then serve hot.

generatedRecipes.title: Harvest Kale Salad with Cranberries and Pepitas

recipe.title: Harvest Kale Salad with Cranberries and Pepitas
recipe.intro: No special equipment needed: a large bowl, a dry skillet, and a small jar or whisk. Wash and dry the kale thoroughly—dry leaves let the dressing cling. Toast the pepitas while you stem and shred the kale so nothing sits idle.
recipe.finish: The salad is best after 20–30 minutes of resting, when the kale has softened but still has some chew. Taste and add a pinch of salt or a splash of cider vinegar if needed, then top with the remaining toasted pepitas and cranberries just before serving for crunch.

ingredients.name: curly kale
ingredients.prep: rinsed, dried, tough stems removed, leaves shredded into bite-size pieces

steps.title: Toast the pepitas
steps.details: Heat a dry medium skillet over medium heat. Add the pepitas and toast, stirring often, until they puff slightly, turn golden, and start popping, 4–6 minutes. Watch closely so they don't scorch. Slide onto a plate to cool.

steps.title: Shred the kale
steps.details: While the pepitas toast, strip the tough stems from the kale and tear or slice the leaves into bite-size pieces. You should have about 8 packed cups. Put the kale in a large bowl.

steps.title: Whisk the vinaigrette
steps.details: In a small jar or bowl, combine the olive oil, cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Shake or whisk until smooth and slightly thickened, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Massage the kale
steps.details: Pour about half the vinaigrette over the kale. With clean hands, rub and squeeze the leaves for 2–3 minutes until they darken, soften, and shrink in volume. This makes raw kale tender and easier to eat.

steps.title: Toss and rest the salad
steps.details: Add half the cranberries and half the cooled pepitas, then toss with the remaining vinaigrette. Let the salad rest at room temperature for 20–30 minutes so the flavors meld and the kale softens further.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.details: Taste the salad and adjust salt or vinegar if needed. Scatter the remaining cranberries and pepitas over the top just before serving.

recipe.title: Skillet Cornbread with Honey Butter
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F with a 10-inch cast-iron skillet inside. Have a whisk, two bowls, and a rubber spatula ready. Let butter soften at room temperature for the honey butter while the oven heats.
recipe.finish: Cornbread is done when golden brown on top and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 20–22 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve warm with the whipped honey butter.

steps.title: Heat oven and skillet
steps.details: Set a rack in the middle and preheat the oven to 425°F. Put a 10-inch cast-iron skillet on the rack to heat for at least 15 minutes.

steps.title: Mix dry ingredients
steps.details: In a large bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until evenly combined.

steps.title: Whisk wet ingredients
steps.details: In a medium bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, and melted butter until smooth and uniform in color.

steps.title: Whip honey butter
steps.details: In a small bowl, mash and stir the softened butter with the honey until pale and fluffy, about 1 minute. Set aside at room temperature.

steps.title: Combine into batter
steps.details: Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and fold with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain; a few small lumps are fine. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Oil the hot skillet
steps.details: Carefully pull out the hot skillet and swirl in the vegetable oil to coat the bottom and sides; it should shimmer.

steps.title: Pour and smooth batter
steps.details: Pour the batter into the hot oiled skillet and spread it evenly with the spatula. It will sizzle slightly at the edges.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.details: Bake at 425°F until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 20–22 minutes.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.details: Cool in the skillet 10 minutes, then cut into wedges. Serve warm with the whipped honey butter and extra honey if desired.

recipe.title: Cranberry Orange Chutney
recipe.intro: A tangy-sweet fall relish. You'll need a medium saucepan, a vegetable peeler or zester, a wooden spoon, and a clean jar. No special equipment. Serve warm or chilled; it thickens as it cools.
recipe.finish: Chutney is done when cranberries have popped and the mixture coats the back of a spoon, about 15 minutes. Cool at least 20 minutes before serving (it thickens further). Taste and adjust sugar or vinegar. Keeps refrigerated up to 2 weeks.

ingredients.name: fresh cranberries
ingredients.prep: rinse; discard soft or shriveled berries

steps.title: Zest and juice orange
steps.details: Zest the orange into a small bowl (1 tbsp). Halve and juice it into a cup (1/2 cup). Remove any seeds.

steps.title: Combine base ingredients
steps.details: In the saucepan, stir together sugar, vinegar, water, cinnamon, ginger, salt, and the orange juice. Add the raisins if using.

steps.title: Add spices, salt, raisins
steps.details: Stir the cinnamon, ginger, salt, and chopped raisins into the saucepan mixture until evenly distributed.

steps.title: Add cranberries and zest
steps.details: Stir in the cranberries and orange zest. The liquid will not cover the berries at first, which is fine.

steps.title: Simmer gently
steps.details: Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer uncovered, stirring every couple of minutes, until berries pop and the mixture thickens, 12 to 15 minutes.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.details: Mash any stubborn whole berries with the spoon. It is ready when a spoon dragged across the pan bottom leaves a brief trail and the chutney is jammy, not watery.

steps.title: Cool and store
steps.details: Remove from heat and cool uncovered 20 minutes. Taste; add a pinch of sugar if too tart or a splash of vinegar if too sweet. Serve warm or refrigerate in a clean jar.

generatedRecipes.title: Pumpkin Spice Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting

recipe.title: Pumpkin Spice Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
recipe.intro: Let eggs and cream cheese come to room temperature. Preheat oven to 350°F and grease two 9-inch round pans, lining bottoms with parchment. You'll need two mixing bowls, a whisk or mixer, and a cooling rack.
recipe.finish: Cake is done when a toothpick in the center comes out clean and the top springs back, about 30–35 minutes; cool completely before frosting. Frost the fully cooled cake, then refrigerate 30 minutes to set. Store covered in the fridge up to 3 days; bring to room temperature before serving.

steps.title: Preheat and grease pans
steps.details: Heat oven to 350°F. Grease two 9-inch round pans and line the bottoms with parchment.

steps.title: Whisk dry ingredients
steps.details: In a large bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt until evenly combined.

steps.title: Mix sugars and oil
steps.details: In a second large bowl, whisk both sugars with the oil until smooth and no dry sugar remains.

steps.title: Add eggs and pumpkin
steps.details: Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the pumpkin and milk until smooth.

steps.title: Fold in dry ingredients
steps.details: Add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and stir just until no flour streaks remain; do not overmix.

steps.title: Bake the cakes
steps.details: Divide batter evenly between the pans. Bake 30–35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean and tops spring back. Cool 10 minutes in pans, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Beat cream cheese frosting
steps.details: While cakes cool, beat softened cream cheese and butter until smooth and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar and vanilla; beat until spreadable.

steps.title: Finish frosting and cool
steps.details: If frosting is soft, chill it 15 minutes. Let cakes cool fully before frosting so it does not melt.

steps.title: Frost the cake
steps.details: Place one cake layer on a plate. Spread about 1/2 cup frosting on top, add the second layer, then cover the top and sides with the remaining frosting.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.details: Refrigerate the frosted cake 30 minutes to set the frosting, then slice and serve.

recipe.title: Spiced Apple Cider
recipe.intro: Use a 4-quart pot or slow cooker. Have a vegetable peeler and a fine-mesh strainer ready. No preheat needed; start the cider first so it can steep while you finish other dishes.
recipe.finish: Cider is ready when fragrant and hot but not boiling. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding spices and peel. Ladle into mugs; add a cinnamon stick or orange slice if you like. Keep any extra warm on low and cool leftovers within 2 hours, then refrigerate up to 3 days.

ingredients.name: orange
ingredients.prep: peel in wide strips with a vegetable peeler, avoiding white pith

ingredients.name: honey or maple syrup
ingredients.prep: optional; omit if cider is already sweet

steps.title: Combine cider and spices
steps.details: Pour the cider into a 4-quart pot. Add the cinnamon sticks, cloves, orange peel, honey if using, nutmeg and salt. Stir once.

steps.title: Warm gently to a simmer
steps.details: Set the pot over medium heat and bring to a bare simmer, small bubbles at the edges only; do not let it boil hard. This takes about 10 minutes from cold.

steps.title: Steep on low
steps.details: Reduce heat to low and keep at a gentle steam for 15 minutes so the spices infuse. The cider should stay hot, around 180-190°F, without rolling bubbles.

steps.title: Taste and strain
steps.details: Taste; steep 5 more minutes if you want a stronger spice flavor. Turn off heat and strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a pitcher or back into the pot, pressing lightly on the solids.

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.details: Ladle into mugs while hot. Add a fresh cinnamon stick or orange slice to each mug if desired.

recipe.title: Slow-Cooker Beef Stew
recipe.intro: Use a 6-quart slow cooker. Have a skillet and cutting board ready; no preheating needed. Trim and cut the beef into 1½-inch chunks, keep pieces similar in size for even cooking.
recipe.finish: The stew is done when the beef shreds easily with a fork and carrots and potatoes are tender, about 8 hours on LOW. Fish out the bay leaves and thyme stems, skim any fat from the surface, taste and add salt and pepper as needed. Serve hot with crusty bread.

ingredients.name: dry red wine or extra beef broth

steps.title: Season and brown beef
steps.details: Pat the beef dry and toss with the salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown half the beef in a single layer, 3–4 minutes per side, until deep brown; transfer to the slow cooker. Repeat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and beef.

steps.title: Soften onion and garlic
steps.details: Lower the skillet heat to medium and add the onion. Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Scrape the mixture into the slow cooker.

steps.title: Bloom tomato paste and flour
steps.details: Add the tomato paste and flour to the hot skillet. Stir constantly for 1–2 minutes until the paste darkens slightly and the flour smells toasted; do not let it burn. Pour in the broth and wine, scraping up browned bits, and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Load slow cooker with liquids
steps.details: Pour the skillet mixture into the slow cooker. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves, and thyme bundle. Push the beef down so it is mostly submerged.

steps.title: Add root vegetables
steps.details: Add the potatoes, carrots, celery, and mushrooms to the slow cooker. Stir gently to distribute them around the beef, keeping everything below the liquid line.

steps.title: Slow cook on low
steps.details: Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours. Avoid lifting the lid so the stew stays hot and cooks evenly.

steps.title: Thicken stew
steps.details: Uncover and remove the bay leaves and thyme bundle. Stir the cornstarch slurry, then stir it into the stew. Cover and cook on HIGH for 10–15 minutes, until the broth is lightly thickened and glossy.

steps.title: Finish with peas
steps.details: Stir in the frozen peas, cover, and let stand off the heat for 5 minutes until heated through. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

recipe.title: Creamy Chicken and Dumplings
recipe.intro: A hearty, comforting dish of shredded chicken in a creamy sauce topped with fluffy drop dumplings. Use a large Dutch oven or heavy pot with a lid. Have all ingredients ready before starting.
recipe.finish: The dumplings are done when they are puffed, cooked through, and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. The sauce should be thick and creamy; if too thin, simmer uncovered for a few minutes. Serve hot, garnished with parsley if desired.

steps.title: Sauté vegetables
steps.details: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add aromatics and chicken
steps.details: Stir in garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper; cook 1 minute. Add chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned, about 4 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer chicken
steps.details: Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature reaches 165°F), about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Shred chicken
steps.details: Transfer chicken to a bowl and shred with two forks. Set aside. Keep the pot with vegetables and broth on the stove.

steps.title: Make creamy sauce
steps.details: In a small bowl, whisk flour with a little milk until smooth. Stir remaining milk and cream into the pot, then whisk in the flour mixture. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Return chicken to pot
steps.details: Stir the shredded chicken back into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Mix dumpling batter
steps.details: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and parsley. Stir in melted butter and milk until just combined (do not overmix).

steps.title: Drop dumplings and cook
steps.details: Drop batter by rounded tablespoonfuls onto simmering chicken mixture, spacing evenly. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Dumplings are done when puffed and a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.details: Turn off heat and let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with parsley if desired and serve hot.

recipe.title: Skillet Cornbread
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F with a 10-inch cast-iron skillet inside. Gather a large bowl, a medium bowl, a whisk, and oven mitts. Have butter ready to melt in the hot skillet.
recipe.finish: Cornbread is done when the top is golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes in the skillet, then slice into wedges and serve warm with extra butter.

steps.title: Heat oven and skillet
steps.details: Set oven to 425°F and put a 10-inch cast-iron skillet on the middle rack to heat for at least 20 minutes.

steps.title: Mix dry ingredients
steps.details: In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until evenly combined.

steps.title: Whisk wet ingredients
steps.details: In a medium bowl, whisk buttermilk and eggs until smooth.

steps.title: Combine batters
steps.details: Pour the buttermilk mixture into the dry ingredients and stir just until no dry streaks remain; small lumps are fine. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Melt butter in skillet
steps.details: Carefully pull the hot skillet out with oven mitts, add butter, and swirl until melted and coating the bottom and sides. Pour the excess butter into the batter and stir it in quickly.

steps.title: Pour batter into skillet
steps.details: With the skillet still hot and buttered, scrape the batter into the center; it should sizzle at the edges and spread evenly.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.details: Bake at 425°F until the top is golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Start checking at 20 minutes.

steps.title: Cool and slice
steps.details: Cool in the skillet on a rack for 10 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and cut into 8 wedges. Serve warm.

recipe.title: Garlic Mashed Potatoes
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 400°F. You'll need a large pot, a baking sheet, and a potato masher or ricer.
recipe.finish: Potatoes are done when fluffy and heated through. Serve hot, garnished with chives if desired.

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.prep: top sliced off to expose cloves

steps.title: Preheat oven and roast garlic
steps.details: Preheat oven to 400°F. Drizzle garlic with olive oil, wrap in foil, and roast until cloves are tender and golden, about 40 minutes.

steps.title: Boil potatoes
steps.details: While garlic roasts, put potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Add 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.

steps.title: Warm dairy and mash potatoes
steps.details: Warm cream and milk in a small saucepan or microwave. Drain potatoes and return to pot. Mash until smooth, then stir in butter, warm cream, milk, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Squeeze roasted garlic
steps.details: Once garlic is cool enough to handle, squeeze cloves out of skins into the potatoes and mix well.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.details: Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with chives if using. Serve hot.

recipe.title: Roasted Root Vegetables with Thyme
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the middle. Use a large rimmed sheet pan or two smaller pans so the vegetables sit in a single layer. Have a wide spatula for turning.
recipe.finish: Vegetables are done when the edges are deeply browned and a parsnip piece pierces easily with a knife, about 35–40 minutes total. Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Transfer to a warm serving bowl and scatter with fresh thyme leaves.

ingredients.name: parsnips
ingredients.prep: peel, cut into 1-inch chunks, remove woody core if large

ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves
ingredients.prep: strip leaves from stems, chop lightly

steps.title: Preheat oven
steps.details: Set oven to 425°F (220°C) with a rack in the middle. Let it heat fully, about 15 minutes, while you prep.

steps.title: Peel and cut roots
steps.details: Peel carrots, parsnips, and sweet potatoes. Cut into even 1-inch chunks so they cook at the same rate; cut any thick parsnip cores out.

steps.title: Toss with oil and seasoning
steps.details: On the sheet pan, toss the cut vegetables with olive oil, salt, and pepper until every piece is lightly coated. Spread into a single layer with space between pieces.

steps.title: Roast first side
steps.details: Roast on the middle rack for 20 minutes without opening the oven. The undersides should be golden brown when you check.

steps.title: Turn and add thyme
steps.details: Remove pan, flip pieces with a spatula, and sprinkle with half the thyme. Return to oven.

steps.title: Roast until tender
steps.details: Roast 15–20 minutes more, until edges are caramelized and a parsnip pierces easily with a knife. Check at 15 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.details: Sprinkle with remaining thyme, taste for salt, and serve hot from a warm bowl.

recipe.title: Classic Caesar Salad
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Gather ingredients: romaine, Parmesan, bread, garlic, lemon, anchovy paste, egg yolk, Dijon, Worcestershire, and olive oil. You'll need a baking sheet, skillet, bowl for dressing, whisk, salad bowl, and a vegetable peeler for shaving Parmesan.
recipe.finish: Toss the romaine with the dressing and croutons just before serving. Top with shaved Parmesan and extra black pepper. Serve immediately.

ingredients.name: romaine lettuce
ingredients.prep: rinsed, dried, and torn into bite-sized pieces

steps.title: Make garlic oil
steps.details: In a small bowl, combine minced garlic and 2 tablespoons olive oil. Let sit 10 minutes to infuse.

steps.title: Toast croutons
steps.details: Toss bread cubes with the garlic oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and bake at 375°F (190°C) until golden and crisp, 12–15 minutes, stirring once.

steps.title: Whisk dressing base
steps.details: In a medium bowl, whisk egg yolk, lemon juice, Dijon, Worcestershire, anchovy paste, salt, and pepper until smooth.

steps.title: Emulsify dressing
steps.details: While whisking constantly, slowly drizzle in remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil until dressing thickens slightly.

steps.title: Toss salad
steps.details: In a large bowl, combine romaine, croutons, and dressing. Toss gently to coat.

steps.title: Finish with Parmesan
steps.details: Top salad with shaved Parmesan and extra black pepper. Serve immediately.

recipe.title: Cheesy Baked Mac and Cheese
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Boil water for pasta. Use a 9x13-inch baking dish. Have a whisk and a large pot ready. Grate the cheeses before starting so the sauce stays smooth.
recipe.finish: The mac and cheese is done when the crumbs are golden and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Let it rest 5–10 minutes so portions hold together. Serve hot as a side for winter comfort food night.

steps.title: Boil pasta until just tender
steps.details: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the macaroni and cook 1 minute less than the package's al dente time, about 6–7 minutes. Drain and set aside.

steps.title: Melt butter for sauce
steps.details: In a large pot over medium heat, melt 3 tablespoons of the butter. Whisk in the flour and cook 1–2 minutes until lightly golden and pasty.

steps.title: Whisk in milk and thicken
steps.details: Slowly pour in the warm milk while whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Cook 5–6 minutes, whisking, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Melt in the cheeses
steps.details: Remove pot from heat. Stir in the cheddar, gruyère, half the parmesan, salt, pepper, and ground mustard until melted and smooth.

steps.title: Combine pasta and sauce
steps.details: Fold the drained macaroni into the cheese sauce until evenly coated. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make buttered breadcrumbs
steps.details: Melt the remaining 1 tablespoon butter. Toss with the panko and the remaining 1/4 cup parmesan in a small bowl.

steps.title: Bake until bubbly and golden
steps.details: Spread the macaroni mixture in a 9x13-inch baking dish and scatter the crumb topping evenly over the top. Bake at 375°F for 20–25 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the sauce bubbles at the edges.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.details: Let the dish rest 5–10 minutes before serving so the sauce sets slightly. Scoop onto plates while hot.

recipe.title: Apple Cinnamon Crumble
recipe.intro: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Have a 9x13-inch baking dish ready. Peel and core apples, and soften butter for the crumble.
recipe.finish: The crumble is done when the topping is golden brown and the apple juices bubble at the edges, about 40–45 minutes. Let it rest 10 minutes before serving warm with vanilla ice cream.

ingredients.name: apples (Granny Smith or Honeycrisp)
ingredients.prep: peeled, cored, and sliced 1/4 inch thick

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.details: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) with a rack in the middle position.

steps.title: Peel and slice apples
steps.details: Peel, core, and slice the apples 1/4 inch thick; you should have about 7 cups.

steps.title: Toss the apple filling
steps.details: In a large bowl, toss the sliced apples with the granulated sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice until evenly coated.

steps.title: Make the crumble topping
steps.details: In a medium bowl, stir together the flour, oats, brown sugar, and salt. Add the cubed cold butter and vanilla. Rub the butter into the dry mixture with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-sized butter bits.

steps.title: Layer the dish
steps.details: Spread the apple mixture evenly in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the apples; do not press it down.

steps.title: Bake the crumble
steps.details: Bake uncovered at 375°F (190°C) until the topping is golden brown and the apple juices bubble at the edges, 40–45 minutes. Cover loosely with foil if the topping browns too quickly.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.details: Let the crumble rest 10 minutes so the filling sets. Scoop into bowls and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

recipe.title: Hot Spiced Apple Cider
